patch.objective: Availability technologies: load-balancing methods, active-active/active-passive high availability, link aggregation, autoscaling, regions/availability zones, and CDNs

sources.cite: CompTIA CloudNetX CNX-001 V1 Exam Objectives, document version 5.0: Network Architecture Design 31%, Network Security 28%, Operations, Monitoring and Performance 16%, Network Troubleshooting 25%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of CompTIA's PDF. Relevant text: 1.4 'Given a scenario, analyze availability requirements to recommend technologies that meet business needs' (load balancing); 2.3 'Given a scenario, configure the appropriate access controls to secure a network' (firewall rules, network security groups); 'Explain the troubleshooting methodology'; 'Given a scenario, troubleshoot connectivity issues' (DNS issues). The objective wording here is the course seed's.

Relevant text: 'By default, requests are distributed between the servers using a weighted round-robin balancing method'; max_fails 'By default, the number of unsuccessful attempts is set to 1'; fail_timeout 'By default, the parameter is set to 10 seconds'; slow_start is listed under 'the following parameters are available as part of our commercial subscription'. Read through summarizing fetches 2026-11-14. The [emerg] message open-source nginx prints for slow_start is authored in nginx's style.

Relevant text: on HUP 'The master process first checks the syntax validity, then tries to apply new configuration ... If this fails, it rolls back changes and continues to work with old configuration. If this succeeds, it starts new worker processes, and sends messages to old worker processes requesting them to shut down gracefully.' Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14. That a restart with an invalid configuration leaves nginx stopped follows from the stop happening before the failed start.

Relevant text: default 'proxy_next_upstream error timeout;'; error, 'an error occurred while establishing a connection with the server, passing a request to it, or reading the response header'. Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14. So a pool member that refuses connections is skipped, not shown to customers: it adds no capacity, and only the error log says so.
